This is wired into generate-agents.py via a --registry=auto|off flag defaulting to auto, and flux-melange's own phases (seed.md, melange-workflow.js) call exactly that script for every round type including STEER-WIDE and FUSE with no override, so they inherit live re-validation by default — never via combine_lenses or search_lenses. So the underlying risk position 2 confirmed is, in the concrete plan, already mitigated. But the brainstorm itself — the ratified record of what mk approved — still names a seam that was never the real one, misleading anyone who reads the brainstorm alone (its own stated audience) rather than the 804-line plan.

claim: The full-text spec that would let the registry recast a clean lens body for free already survives inside the registry design (data/generated/specs/<id>.json, undeleted by Fork 4's prune), and the only function that already reads it correctly (embedding_text) is not the function that serves a reuse hit — materialize() copies the harvested, sanitizer-truncated body verbatim instead.
evidence: Read this lens's own spec file directly: its review_areas array holds six strings of 748-1081 characters, all fully intact — well above the 200-char max_item_len that produced this file's six '[truncated — N chars omitted]' markers (.claude/agents/fd-hand-composition-foul-case.md:36,41,46,51,56,61). sanitize_untrusted.py:156 is the only place that builds the marker string, and generate-agents.py's render_agent calls it fresh from spec.get('review_areas') on every render — meaning the truncation is a deterministic render-time artifact of the full spec text, not data loss at the source. The plan's harvest/embed.py (L568) already prefers spec over body for embedding text when a spec exists, but materialize() (L655) is documented to write 'registry body' — the stored, already-truncated .md — verbatim, only overriding frontmatter fields, never re-rendering from the co-located specs/<id>.json.

evidence: grep -n 'domains:' .claude/agents/*.md shows 5 of 6 files in this repo carry domains: ["uncategorized"]; generate-agents.py:192 (return sorted(domains) if domains else ["uncategorized"]) is the only fallback branch, fed by a fixed ~24-entry filename-segment map. remediation: Add a domains_source: "inferred" | "default" flag to render_agent's frontmatter and thread it through scan.py/merge.py's domains union so harvest and lexicalScore can down-weight or skip the default case.

claim: New insight from the contradiction: even once Stage D lands exactly as planned, its resolve() gate only ever sees SEED/FUSE/STEER-WIDE lens generation through generate-agents.py; DEEPEN and PROBE-DISAGREEMENT directives (priority #2 and #1 in the controller's own selection policy, routinely the majority of a round once STEER-WIDE's novelty gate starts skipping it) re-dispatch an already-existing lens with no spec and no generate-agents.py call, so 'reuse-before-regenerate' as described structurally can't reach roughly half of a typical melange round's lens traffic.

Selection priority (retarget.md:24-27): PROBE-DISAGREEMENT first, DEEPEN second, FUSE third, STEER-WIDE conditional. Worked example (directive-vocabulary.md:79): STEER-WIDE skipped, its budget reallocated to DEEPEN. Only seed.md:19, melange-workflow.js:1003 (FUSE) and :1037 (STEER-WIDE) call generate-agents.py — the one path Task 17 patches.
remediation: Scope the brainstorm's reuse-before-regenerate coverage claim (L24-27, L35-36) to name which melange directive types it can ever reach (SEED/FUSE/STEER-WIDE lens generation) versus which it structurally cannot (DEEPEN/PROBE-DISAGREEMENT reuse of already-materialized lenses), so a reader doesn't assume registry dedupe applies to every lens a melange run touches.
